posts.title: How to choose your wedding photographer — 7 questions
posts.caption:
Your photographer is the one vendor you can't re-do. The cake gets eaten, the flowers wilt — the photos are what's left. So vet them like it matters.

Seven questions that go past the portfolio: can I see a full gallery, not the highlight reel? What's your backup if you get sick? How are the files protected? When do I get them? Is there a second shooter — and who? What does the contract actually cover? Do I get everything?

The honest one hides under all of them: do I feel like myself around you? That's what shows up in the photos. Full guide on the journal — link in bio. 🤍

posts.title: The Fairmont Hotel Vancouver — Jayleen & Ryan
posts.caption:
Marble, gold, and a wall of orchids. The Fairmont Hotel Vancouver doesn't need much help looking like a wedding — the room does half the work, the light does the rest.

Jayleen & Ryan went full black-tie: a gilded ballroom, a staircase made for a dress, the kind of timeless that doesn't date. If you want your day elevated without trying too hard, there isn't a more beautiful ballroom in the city.

📍 Fairmont Hotel Vancouver · Full wedding on the journal — link in bio.

posts.title: Not photo people? — directing camera-shy couples
posts.caption:
"We're not really photo people." We hear it on every first call — and honestly? Good.

The couples who think they're awkward end up with the realest photos. The stiffness isn't you, it's being told to "just act natural" while someone points a lens at your face. So we don't pose you. We give you something to do and someone to look at, and we disappear. The first ten minutes feel weird for everyone. Then you forget we're there — and that's where the good ones live.

You don't have to be photogenic. You just have to show up. How we direct camera-shy couples — full post on the journal, link in bio.
